landing.meta.title: Link — Speak after class. Link does the follow-up.
landing.meta.description: Link connects parents, teachers and centres across Egypt. Parents find and pay teachers, teachers rent halls, and centres fill empty slots. After class, a short Arabic voice note becomes student records, flags who is slipping, and a WhatsApp update your staff approve.
landing.faq.q1: Do teachers need to type anything?
landing.faq.a1: No. Attendance is a few taps, and a short voice note in Egyptian Arabic covers the rest. Teachers can type instead if they prefer. Either way, the teacher checks and confirms before anything is saved.
landing.faq.q2: How accurate is the Arabic transcription?
landing.faq.a2: It makes mistakes, especially with names and numbers. That's why the teacher sees every item to accept, edit or skip, and Link never guesses a student. In a pilot, voice is switched on for a teacher only after we check it on your centre's own notes.
landing.faq.a3: No. Link drafts the message; a staff member checks and approves every one. In the pilot, your staff send the approved text from your centre's own WhatsApp.
landing.join.lead: Tell us about your centre. We'll contact you to plan a free pilot of about 7 days.

site.nav.label: Main
site.hero.lead: Link connects parents, teachers and centres across Egypt. Parents find and pay teachers, teachers rent halls, and centres fill empty slots. After class, a short Arabic voice note becomes student records, flags who is slipping, and a WhatsApp update your staff approve.
site.hero.visualLabel: How one class becomes a follow-up: a voice note, a confirmed record, a flag and an approved WhatsApp update (sample data)
site.hero.altVoice: Voice note from Ms. Heba, Maths, Grade 9, 0:42, transcribed: Omar understands the explanation but gets lost in the steps when he solves alone.
site.hero.altRecord: Record created for Omar Hassan: attendance present, quiz 14 out of 20, understanding partial, teacher confirmed.
site.hero.altFlag: Flag, attendance: 2 absences in a row, assigned to Mona at the front desk, call today.
site.hero.altWhatsApp: WhatsApp update to Omar's parent, approved by Mona at 6:40 pm: Omar attended today and scored 14 out of 20; next class we'll review the problem-solving steps with him.
site.principles.arabicBody: Built for Egyptian Arabic voice notes, not translated English forms.
site.principles.peopleBody: Teachers confirm records. Staff approve every parent message.
site.principles.rulesBody: Every flag shows the rule that raised it. No black-box scores.
site.principles.whatsappBody: Updates reach parents where they already are.
site.problem.title: A concern is noticed. Then nobody follows up.
site.problem.body: In most centres, what a teacher notices lives in their head, on a paper register or somewhere in a WhatsApp group. Nobody owns the next step, and by the time someone connects the dots the student has already stopped coming.
site.problem.answer: Link gives every concern an owner and a due date.
site.problem.step1Title: Teacher notices Omar is lost on multi-step problems
site.problem.step1Body: Mentioned in the staff room. Never written down.
site.problem.step2Body: Nobody links it to what the teacher saw.
site.problem.step3Body: Recorded on paper. No one is assigned to call home.
site.problem.step4Title: His parent moves him to another centre
site.problem.step4Body: The centre finds out when the fees stop.
site.problem.withLink: With Link: after week 2 the rule “2 absences in a row” flags Omar, Mona at the front desk is assigned to call home, and his parent gets an approved WhatsApp update the same day.
site.how.title: From a voice note to a parent update, in four steps
site.how.lead: Teachers don't fill in forms. Staff don't chase paper. Everyone can see what happens next.
site.how.speakBody: After class the teacher records a short note in Egyptian Arabic on their phone. It works offline and uploads later.
site.how.confirmBody: Link transcribes the note and pulls out attendance, scores and concerns for each student. The teacher checks and confirms.
site.how.confirmAlt: Omar H.: present, 14/20. Salma A.: absent.
site.how.flagBody: Rules you can read flag students who are slipping: missed classes, falling scores, repeated concerns.
site.how.flagAlt: Rule: 2 absences in a row. Salma A., raised today.
site.how.followBody: Each flag becomes a task with an owner and a due date. Parent updates are drafted for staff to approve.
site.how.followAlt: Call Salma's parent, today. Mona: outcome logged.
site.product.title: One place to see who needs attention today
site.product.lead: Owners see every flag, who owns it and what happened. Teachers get a simple phone app. Parents get updates on WhatsApp.
site.product.calloutRule: Every flag shows the rule behind it
site.product.calloutConfirm: Teachers confirm what the AI understood
site.product.altOwner: Owner dashboard, Today: 3 follow-ups due, 1 overdue action, 2 missing session records, 6 of 8 records complete; follow-up cards for Mariam Hassan and Omar Ali.
site.product.altTeacher: Teacher app, Here's what I understood: attendance, scores and an observation from a 38-second voice note, waiting for the teacher to confirm and save.
site.features.title: Everything a centre needs to act early
site.features.lead: Built for multi-teacher tutoring centres, where concerns fall between teachers, front desk and parents.
site.features.rulesBody: Choose the rules that matter to your centre. Every flag shows exactly which rule raised it, so staff trust it and parents get a clear reason.
site.features.rulesAlt: Three rules: 2 absences in a row flags attendance to the front desk the same day; quiz score falls 2 times running flags progress to the teacher within 3 days; same concern noted 3 times flags understanding to the head of subject this week.
site.features.voiceBody: Teachers speak the way they talk after class, English subject terms included. No forms to fill in.
site.features.recordsBody: Attendance, scores and observations for each student, checked by the teacher before anything is saved.
site.features.ownerBody: Every concern gets a person and a due date. Outcomes are logged, so nothing quietly disappears.
site.features.dashboardBody: Open follow-ups, overdue actions and missing records across every teacher and group, in one view.
site.features.updatesBody: Link drafts a short WhatsApp message in Arabic from the teacher's note. Staff edit and approve it. Nothing reaches a parent without a person saying yes.
site.features.updatesAlt: Draft to Salma's parent: Good evening, Salma missed two classes in a row; we'd like to check on her and see how to make up the last lesson. Buttons: Edit, Approve & send.
site.features.bilingualBody: Every screen works in Arabic, right to left, and in English. Staff choose their language.

site.faq.title: Questions centres ask us
site.faq.body: Can't find what you need? Send us a message and we'll walk you through how Link would work at your centre or for your groups.
site.faq.q1: Do teachers need to type anything?
site.faq.a1: No. Teachers record a short voice note in Egyptian Arabic after class. Link turns it into records, and the teacher checks and confirms them before they're saved.
site.faq.q2: How accurate is the Arabic transcription?
site.faq.a2: We're testing accuracy on real teacher notes during the pilot. That's why teachers confirm every record and staff approve every message before anything reaches a parent.
site.faq.a3: No. Link drafts the WhatsApp update from the teacher's note. A member of your staff edits and approves it before it's sent.
site.faq.a4: Joining is free for centres, teachers and parents. Link keeps a small marketing fee from hall rent paid through Link (for example 5–10%) and a small commission on each paid booking, taken from the teacher's fee. AI follow-up and analytics are an optional monthly subscription.
site.faq.q5: How does money move in the marketplace?
site.faq.a5: Everything goes through Link. Parents pay the teacher by card, Fawry or mobile wallet, and teachers pay hall rent through Link. Link deducts its fees and pays teachers and centres on a set schedule, so nobody chases cash.
site.faq.q6: Who can see our centre's data?
site.faq.a6: Only your centre's staff, with access based on their role. Each centre's data is kept separate from every other centre.
